In summary, our research is concerned with

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for 28 analytes, the RIs were derived as gender-specific (TC, HDLC, TG, HDL-C/TG, hsCRP), and for another five analytes (ALB, AST, ALP, CK, and Urea), age-specific RIs were required, and for one analyte, (Glu), age-specific RIS was required.
RIs for 18 analytes are gender independent, 4 analytes are age dependent, and 11 are gender and age dependent.
RIs derived by parametric methods without LAVE procedure should be the preferred choice for the Indian population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RIs derived in this study are generally applicable for the healthy Indians.
the C-RIDL protocol is a robust approach to establish country-specific RIs.
the RIs in this report should be considered as the first step for the implementation of country specific reference intervals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RIs should be derived by the parametric method, which can be more informative for clinicians.
the RIs derived by parametric methods without LAVE are generally more appropriate than those by non-parametric methods with LAVE.
RIs derived by parametric and nonparametric methods may differ significantly and the former may be narrower.
